source_text: ἀλλ' εὐθύμους καὶ ἱλαροὺς τῆς ἐν Χριστῷ πολιτείας ἐξῆφθαι πρέπει. Τοῦτο γὰρ, οἶμαι, ἔστι τὸ, «Δεῦτε ἀγαλλιασώμεθα τῷ Κυρίῳ.» Ἐπιλάμψει γὰρ οὕτω καθαρῶς τε καὶ ἐναργῶς ἡ δόξα Χριστοῦ, ἀσμενέστατα προσιεμένη τὰς τῶν ἁγίων καρποφορίας, καθάπερ ἀμέλει καὶ τότε Θεὸς ἐν εἴδει πυρὸς καταπεφοίτηκεν ἐναργῶς, καὶ κατέφαγε τὰ θύματα. Μόνον δὲ οὐχὶ τροφὴν ἡγεῖται καὶ τρυφὴν τῶν ἡγιασμένων ἐν πίστει τὴν εὐδοκίμησιν. Ὑπεμφαίνει δέ τι καὶ μυστικὸν ὁ λόγος· τότε μὲν γὰρ ἐπὶ τὰ διχοτομήματα τὴν πυρὸς ἀκμὴν καθίει Θεὸς, οἱονεί πως τῶν προκειμένων ἁπτόμενος· ὑποπλάττεται γὰρ τὴν πυρὸς φύσιν ἀεὶ τὸ Θεῖον. Νυνὶ δὲ τῆς νοητῆς προτιθεμένης αὐτῷ θυσίας, οὐκ ἐν εἴδει πυρὸς, ἀλλ' ἐν ἁγίῳ Πνεύματι, τῶν προκειμένων νοητῶς ἐφαπτόμενος, ζωοποιὸν ἀποφαίνει τοῖς ἐφιεμένοις μεταλαχεῖν, καὶ ἀληθὲς ἐν πίστει τὸ χρῆμα δεδέγμεθα. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ὀρθῶς ἔφης. {ΚΥΡ.} Ἐξάρας δὲ Ἀαρὼν τὰς χεῖρας ηὐλόγησε τὸν λαόν. Καὶ θέα δὴ πάλιν ὡς ἐν πρώτῃ χειρῶν ἐπιθέσει ἐπὶ λαοῖς διὰ τοῦ Ἀαρών· εὐλογεῖ γὰρ ἅπαντας ὁ ἀληθὴς Ἀαρὼν, ἱερέας καὶ λαοὺς, τοὺς μικροὺς μετὰ τῶν μεγάλων, κατὰ τὸ γεγραμμένον, μονονουχὶ καὶ χεῖρας ἐπιθεὶς, καὶ σημεῖον ἂν γένοιτο σαφὲς ἡ χειρὸς ἐπίθεσις τῆς τοῦ παναγίου Πνεύματος εἰς ἡμᾶς καταβολῆς. Πρὸ δὲ τῆς ἱερουργίας τῆς Ἀαρὼν ἡ χειρῶν ἐπίθεσις οὐκ ἦν. «Οὔπω γὰρ ἦν Πνεῦμα,» κατὰ τὴν Ἰωάννου φωνὴν, ὅτι «Ἰησοῦς οὐδέπω ἐδοξάσθη.» {ΠΑΛΛ.} Πιθανὸς ὁ λόγος. {ΚΥΡ.} Καὶ τόνδε τῆς ἱερέων εὐχῆς καταῤῥυθμίζει τρόπον, προαναγορεύσεις τινὰς τῶν διὰ Χριστοῦ παθημάτων εὖ μάλα τιθεὶς τοὺς ἐν αὐτῇ λόγους. Ἔφη γὰρ, ὅτι «Λάλησον Ἀαρὼν καὶ τοῖς υἱοῖς αὐτοῦ λέγων· Οὕτως εὐλογήσετε τοὺς υἱοὺς Ἰσραὴλ, λέγοντες αὐτοῖς. Καὶ ἐπιθήσουσι τὸ ὄνομά μου ἐπὶ τοὺς υἱοὺς Ἰσραὴλ, καὶ ἐγὼ Κύριος εὐλογήσω αὐτοὺς, Εὐλογήσαι σε Κύριος καὶ φυλάξαι σε, ἐπιφάναι Κύριος τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ σὲ, καὶ δώῃ σοι εἰρήνην, καὶ ἐλεησάτω σε.» Προστάττει μὲν οὖν εὐλογεῖν τὸν λαὸν τοὺς ἐν ἱερωσύνῃ κατεστεμμένους, ἀφίστησι δὲ χρησίμως εἰκαιότητος λογισμῶν, οὐκ ἀνθρώπου χεῖρα τὴν εὐλογοῦσαν δεικνὺς, ἀλλ' ἑαυτὸν ὡς Κύριον. «Πᾶσα γὰρ δόσις ἀγαθὴ, καὶ πᾶν δώρημα ἀγαθὸν, καὶ πᾶσα εὐλογία ἄνωθέν ἐστι καταβαίνουσα ἀπὸ τοῦ Πατρὸς τῶν φώτων,» κατὰ τὸ γεγραμμένον. Χριστὸς δὲ τῆς εὐλογίας ἡ ὁδὸς, καὶ αὐτός ἐστιν ἡμῖν τῶν οὐρανίων ἀγαθῶν ὁ διανομεὺς, ἐν αὐτῷ τε καὶ δι' αὐτοῦ τὰ πάντα παρὰ τοῦ Πατρός. Καὶ γοῦν ὁ θεσπέσιος Παῦλος, «Χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη, φησὶν, ἀπὸ Θεοῦ Πατρὸς ἡμῶν, καὶ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.» Εὐλογούμεθα δὴ οὖν ἐν ὀνόματι Θεοῦ, πῶς δ' ἂν γένοιτο τυχὸν καὶ ὁ τοῦδε τρόπος, κατασημαίνων ἀστείως, ἐπιφθέγγεσθαι δεῖν ἔφη τὸν ἐπευχόμενον ἱερέα· «Εὐλογήσαι σε Κύριος καὶ φυλάξαι σε, ἐπι
pass_a_gloss: [continuing 23: 'for not gloomy and tearful,'] but cheerful (εὔθυμος) and glad (ἱλαρός) it befits (πρέπει) to have been attached (ἐξάπτω, pf. inf. ἐξῆφθαι) to the citizenship/way of life (πολιτεία) in Christ. For this, I think, is the: 'Come, let us exult (ἀγαλλιάομαι) to the Lord.' For thus the glory of Christ will shine upon (ἐπιλάμπω) purely and clearly, most gladly (ἀσμενέστατα) accepting (προσίημι) the fruit-bearings (καρποφορία) of the saints, just as indeed then God came down (καταφοιτάω) in form (εἶδος) of fire visibly (ἐναργῶς), and devoured the victims. He all but considers (ἡγέομαι) as food (τροφή) and luxury/delight (τρυφή) the good repute/approved conduct (εὐδοκίμησις) of those sanctified in faith. The account also hints (ὑπεμφαίνω) something mystical (μυστικός): for then upon the halves/cut pieces (διχοτόμημα) God sent down (καθίημι) the edge/vigor (ἀκμή) of fire, as it were somehow touching (ἅπτομαι) the things lying before (πρόκειμαι); for the Divine (τὸ Θεῖον) always feigns/assumes (ὑποπλάττομαι) the nature (φύσις) of fire. But now, the intelligible/spiritual (νοητός) sacrifice being set before (προτίθημι) him, not in form of fire but in Holy Spirit (Πνεῦμα ἅγιον), touching (ἐφάπτομαι) the things set before intelligibly (νοητῶς), he shows [it] life-giving (ζωοποιός) to those desiring (ἐφίημι) to partake (μεταλαμβάνω), and we have received (δέχομαι) the thing as true in faith. PALL: You said rightly. CYR: Aaron having lifted up the hands blessed the people. And behold (θέα) again as in a first laying-on of hands (χειρῶν ἐπίθεσις) upon peoples through Aaron; for the true (ἀληθής) Aaron blesses all, priests and peoples, the small with the great, according to what is written, all but also laying on hands; and the laying-on of the hand would become a clear sign (σημεῖον) of the sending-down (καταβολή) of the all-holy (πανάγιος) Spirit to us. Before the sacred service (ἱερουργία) of Aaron the laying-on of hands was not. 'For not yet was Spirit,' according to the voice of John, 'because Jesus not yet was glorified (δοξάζω).' PALL: The account is persuasive (πιθανός). CYR: And he regulates (καταρρυθμίζω) this manner (τρόπος) of the prayer (εὐχή) of priests, setting the words in it very well as certain foretellings (προαναγόρευσις) of the things experienced (πάθημα) through Christ. For he said: 'Speak to Aaron and his sons saying: Thus you will bless the sons of Israel, saying to them. And they will put my name (ὄνομα) upon the sons of Israel, and I the Lord will bless them. May the Lord bless you and guard (φυλάσσω) you, may the Lord make appear (ἐπιφαίνω) his face (πρόσωπον) upon you, and give you peace (εἰρήνη), and let him have mercy (ἐλεέω) on you.' He commands those crowned (καταστέφω) in priesthood to bless the people, and he usefully (χρησίμως) removes (ἀφίστημι) [them] from rashness (εἰκαιότης) of reasonings (λογισμός), showing not a hand of man as the one blessing, but himself as Lord. 'For every good giving (δόσις) and every good gift (δώρημα) and every blessing (εὐλογία) is from above coming down from the Father of lights,' according to what is written. Christ is the way (ὁδός) of the blessing, and he is for us the distributor (διανομεύς) of the heavenly goods, in him and through him all things from the Father. Indeed the inspired Paul: 'Grace (χάρις) to you and peace, he says, from God our Father and our Lord Jesus Christ.' We are blessed then in the name of God; and how perhaps the manner of this would come about, signifying elegantly, he said the praying priest must utter over (ἐπιφθέγγομαι): 'May the Lord bless you and guard you, may the Lord make appear [continues in 25]'.
pass_b_english: Cyril: …but in good cheer and gladness that we ought to hold fast to the life in Christ. For this, I think, is the meaning of ‘Come, let us rejoice in the Lord’ (Psalm 95:1). For so the glory of Christ will shine out purely and clearly, welcoming most gladly the fruits the saints bring, just as then, too, God came down visibly in the form of fire and consumed the sacrifices (Leviticus 9:24). He all but counts the approved life of those sanctified in faith as his food and delight. The passage also hints at a mystery. For then God sent the blaze of fire down upon the divided pieces, as though in some way touching what lay before him, for the Godhead always takes on the guise of fire. But now, when the spiritual sacrifice is set before him, he touches what lies before him in a spiritual way, not in the form of fire but in the Holy Spirit, and makes it life-giving for those who desire to partake of it; and we have received this by faith as true.

Cyril: Aaron lifted up his hands and blessed the people (Leviticus 9:22). And see again: here, through Aaron, is as it were the first laying on of hands upon the people. For the true Aaron blesses everyone, priests and people, the small together with the great, as it is written (Psalm 115:13), all but laying his hands on them as well; and the laying on of the hand would be a clear sign of the all-holy Spirit coming down upon us. Before Aaron's priestly service there was no laying on of hands. ‘For the Spirit was not yet,’ as John says, ‘because Jesus was not yet glorified’ (John 7:39).

Cyril: He also sets in order the form of the priests' prayer in this way, making its words very aptly foretell something of what would come to us through Christ. For he said: ‘Speak to Aaron and his sons, saying: Thus you shall bless the sons of Israel, saying to them. And they shall put my name upon the sons of Israel, and I the Lord will bless them. May the Lord bless you and keep you; may the Lord make his face shine upon you, and give you peace, and have mercy on you’ (Numbers 6:23–27). So he commands those crowned with the priesthood to bless the people, but he usefully keeps them from rash thinking by showing that it is not a human hand that blesses, but he himself, as Lord. For ‘every good gift and every good present and every blessing is from above, coming down from the Father of lights,’ as it is written (James 1:17). And Christ is the way of the blessing; he is the one who distributes the heavenly goods to us, and in him and through him all things come from the Father. Indeed the inspired Paul says, ‘Grace to you and peace from God our Father and our Lord Jesus Christ’ (Romans 1:7). So we are blessed in the name of God; and, aptly indicating how this too might come about, he said that the priest who prays over the people must pronounce: ‘May the Lord bless you and keep you; may the Lord make…’ (Numbers 6:24–25)
